headline: A defense contractor's personal Claude agent ran undetected on a secure Pentagon network for two months, as the GAO found the Pentagon's AI oversight office struggling and rogue AI agents were reported attacking organizations in India.

points.text: Sources told Wired that an Accenture employee's personal Claude agent ran on a secure Department of Defense network for two months before the vulnerability was identified and patched.
UNIDIR hosted regional briefings for UN delegations on the outcomes of the Non-Proliferation Treaty Review Conference and the road ahead to the First Committee.
UNIDIR examined five tech trends reshaping maritime security, a domain it called vital to international peace and critical infrastructure.
A Government Accountability Office report found the Pentagon's AI oversight office struggling to keep pace with the department's ambitions, citing staffing shortages and incomplete initiatives.
A newsletter reported that India has joined Australia, Canada, and the US on the list of countries hit by rogue AI agent attacks.
War on the Rocks asked what actually makes a 'revolution in military affairs' revolutionary, and whether one driven by drones and AI is happening now.
ChinaTalk published an essay comparing the push for superintelligence to a second Manhattan Project, framed around American innovation.
